questions.question: May you drop off a passenger for 10 seconds on crossing zig-zag lines?
options: No, stopping and parking are banned on the zig-zags
Yes, if you stay in the car
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking or waiting on crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: If you want to go straight across a box junction, what must be clear first?
options: The exit road on the far side of the box
Nothing if the light is green
questions.explain: Rule 174: Your exit must be clear before entering a box junction.

questions.question: How much room should you give a cyclist when overtaking at 25 mph?
questions.explain: Rule 163: At least 1.5 metres at speeds up to 30 mph.

questions.question: In dry weather, what is the two-second rule used for?
options: Keeping a safe stopping gap behind the vehicle ahead
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 uses the two-second rule to keep a safe gap.

questions.question: Who needs to see your signal before you turn?
options: Other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians nearby
questions.explain: Rule 103: Signals warn all road users of your plans.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a signed 20 mph zone?
questions.explain: Rule 124: Obeying signed speed limits including 20 mph zones.

questions.question: What is the red and amber phase useful for while you wait behind the line?
options: Getting ready to move off safely once green appears
questions.explain: Rule 175: Use red and amber to prepare to move off and check around you. Not to cross the line early.

questions.question: What shape is a red-and-white Give Way sign?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 uses the inverted red-and-white triangle for Give Way.

questions.question: A person with a white cane is waiting. At a side road you plan to turn into. What should you do?
options: Stop in good time and give way
questions.explain: Rule H2: Give extra care. Patience to pedestrians who may need more time to cross.

questions.question: Why should you not swing out to the right before turning left?
options: Rule 182 warns it misleads following drivers and risks a crash
questions.explain: Rule 182 says not to swing out to the right before a left turn.

questions.question: What should you do right after checking your mirrors before changing lanes?
options: Check your blind spot over your shoulder
questions.explain: Rule 133: To check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do after you finish overtaking on a two-way road?
options: Move back to the left as soon as it is safe
questions.explain: Rule 160: Return to the left side smoothly once you are safely past.

questions.question: What road marking sits across each entrance to a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 marks roundabout entrances with broken give-way lines.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when taking an exit to the right?
options: No signal until after you leave
questions.explain: Rule 186: To signal right on approach for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: What signal must you give just before leaving any roundabout?
questions.explain: Rule 186: A left signal as you prepare to leave a roundabout.

questions.question: In which direction do all roundabouts flow in Great Britain?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require clockwise travel on UK roundabouts.

questions.question: When the lights turn green and cyclists are inside the ASL box. What should you do?
options: Give them time and space to move off safely
Edge into the box behind them
questions.explain: Rule 178: Let cyclists pull away safely and leave plenty of room when passing.

questions.question: Where must you stop when a traffic light is red?
options: In the middle of the crossroads
questions.explain: Rule 175: You must keep all of your vehicle behind the white stop line.

questions.question: Why should you look again for motorcycles before turning right?
options: They are small and can be hidden behind cars
They must stop for turning cars
questions.explain: Rule 180: Watch carefully for motorcycles and cyclists coming towards you.

questions.question: On a two-lane roundabout, where should you position your car?
options: Centred cleanly inside your marked lane
Hugging the grass island on every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to keep cleanly within their lane markings.

questions.question: Does a flashing amber light at a pelican. Crossing mean the same as a steady amber light?
options: No, flashing amber means give way to pedestrians on the crossing
questions.explain: Rule 196: At a pelican crossing. Flashing amber means let any pedestrians finish crossing, then go if clear.

questions.question: If you approach a roundabout in the wrong lane. Traffic is beside you, what is safest?
options: Follow your lane safely and turn around later
Cut across the car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 avoids sudden lane changes across circulating traffic.

questions.question: When can the right-hand approach lane also be used for going straight ahead?
options: When road signs or lane arrows direct straight-ahead traffic into that lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 notes that signs and markings can override the default left lane.

questions.question: Does the zig-zag no-overtaking rule apply at signal-controlled crossings like pelican crossings too?
options: Yes, it applies at all pedestrian crossings with zig-zags
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies to zebra, pelican, puffin, and toucan crossings with zig-zags.

questions.question: What should you do if a car in front stops inside a box junction. Leaves no room on the far side?
options: Wait behind the box line until space opens past the box
Drive onto the yellow lines behind them
questions.explain: Rule 174: Waiting outside the box until your exit is clear.

questions.question: If a large lorry is in front of you, why should you stay well back?
options: So you can see past it and its driver can see you in their mirrors
To stay in its blind spot
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 helps you stay visible and see further ahead.

questions.question: If you want to turn into a side road just past a parked car. When do you signal left?
options: After passing the parked car so nobody thinks you are stopping
questions.explain: Rule 103: Early signals near parked cars can mislead others.

questions.question: What does a round white sign with a black diagonal stripe mean?
questions.explain: Rule 124: links the national speed limit sign to 60 or 70 mph limits.

questions.question: Before turning left soon after passing a cyclist, what must you check?
options: Do not overtake and immediately cut across the cyclist's path
Always turn sharply in front of them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 182 warn against 'left hooks' across cyclists.

questions.question: When turning left into a side road, where should you look for waiting pedestrians?
options: Along the pavement and crossing point of the side road
questions.explain: Rule H2: Scan the side road pavement early before you start steering into the turn.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes without checking your blind spot?
options: You could hit a cyclist, rider, or car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 highlights that motorcycles and cars can hide in blind spots.

questions.question: If you pass a row of parked cars on your left. What should you do afterwards?
options: Return to the left when there is room
questions.explain: Rule 160: Move back to the left once past the parked cars. So oncoming traffic has space.

questions.question: What should you also watch for before entering a roundabout besides cars?
options: Cyclists, motorcyclists, and pedestrians crossing the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds drivers to watch out for cyclists, riders, and pedestrians.

questions.question: If you signal right on approach, which exit are you telling others you want?
options: An exit to the right (past straight ahead)
The first exit on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses a right approach signal for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: What should you check in your mirrors just. Before signalling left to leave an inner roundabout lane?
options: Check your left mirror and blind spot for cars or cyclists beside you
Only look at the central island
questions.explain: Rule 186: To watch for traffic on your left before moving out to exit.

questions.question: At a painted mini-roundabout, how should you pass the white circle when turning right?
options: Drive clockwise around the painted circle if possible
Cut straight across the wrong side of the circle
questions.explain: Rule 188: and Rule 185 state all vehicles must pass around the central marking clockwise.

questions.question: Why should you not stop inside the cycle box. Even if no cyclist is there yet?
options: Cyclists may ride up the left side to use it
questions.explain: Rule 178: Cyclists filter forward to reach the box safely before the lights change.

questions.question: The light is red, and there is a green left filter arrow lit. What may you do?
options: Turn left if safe, watching for pedestrians
questions.explain: Rule 177: allows you to move only in the direction of the green filter arrow.

questions.question: If parked cars block your view at a Give Way line, what should you do?
options: Edge forward slowly until you can see clearly
questions.explain: Rule 172: Creeping forward safely when parked vehicles block sightlines.

questions.question: An oncoming car flashes its headlights as you wait to turn right. What does it mean?
options: It is definitely safe to turn
Only that the other driver is warning you they are there
questions.explain: Rule 180 and Rule 110: Never treat a flash as a safe invitation.

questions.question: Are half-box junctions sometimes painted on only one side of a T-junction?
options: Yes, to keep that side clear for turning traffic
No, they are always full squares
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 covers full and half-box yellow markings at busy junctions.

questions.question: At 60 mph, roughly how far does a car travel in two seconds?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 shows two seconds scales automatically with higher speed.

questions.question: You see a car approaching from the right with its left indicator on. What should you do?
options: Wait until you are sure it is actually turning before pulling out
questions.explain: Rule 172: Never to assume a flashing indicator means the driver will turn.

questions.question: Why must you watch the outer lane carefully when joining a two-lane roundabout?
options: A driver in the inner lane might switch outward or a cyclist might be riding there
The outer lane is always closed
questions.explain: Rule 185: Watching all circulating lanes and cyclists before entering.

questions.question: Why do some large roundabouts paint route numbers like 'M6' inside the approach lanes?
options: To help you pick the right lane early for your destination
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide drivers cleanly through big junctions.

questions.question: If a main road has two lanes in one direction. You turn left onto it, which lane should you join?
options: The left-hand lane unless road signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Rule 172: and lane rules keep turning traffic in the left lane when clear.

questions.question: On a spiral roundabout, how do the lane markings guide you?
options: They gradually lead you outward toward your exit
They mean you must stop on the island
questions.explain: Rule 186: Following lane markings that guide you cleanly out to your exit.

questions.question: What should you do if a lorry beside. You needs extra width to turn on a roundabout?
options: Hold back and give the lorry plenty of room instead of sitting alongside it
Pull right beside its rear wheels
questions.explain: Rule 186: and 221 warn that long vehicles swing wide across lanes on roundabouts.

questions.question: May you cross a solid white centre line to pass a cyclist?
options: Only if the cyclist is travelling at 10 mph or less and the way ahead is clear
Yes, at any speed on blind bends
questions.explain: Rule 129: and Rule 163 allow crossing a solid line. To pass a cyclist at 10 mph or less when clear.

questions.question: When you are stopped in a queue. Where should you wait if space ends at a zebra crossing?
options: Before the stripes so the crossing stays clear
On top of the black and white stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 and 192 keep crossings clear for people on foot.
